questions.text: Rearrange the expression 2y = ∛(3x + 5) to make x the subject.

Consider the graph of y = 2x² + ax + b, where a and b are constants. The graph crosses the x-axis at (3, 0). The point (–1, 16) also lies on the graph.

Find the values of a and b.

A rectangle is inscribed in a circle with radius r. The length of the rectangle is twice its width.

Find a fully simplified expression for the area of the rectangle in terms of r.
questions.markingGuide: Width = w, length = 2w. Diagonal = 2r. w² + 4w² = 4r². 5w² = 4r². w² = 4r²/5. Area = 2w² = 8r²/5.

2^(2x+1) = 2·(2^x)² = 2n². 2^(x+3) = 8·2^x = 8n. Equation: 2n² – 40 = 8n → 2n² – 8n – 40 = 0 → n² – 4n – 20 = 0. Hmm: (n–?). Disc = 16+80 = 96. Not clean. Let me adjust: 2^(2x+1) – 72 = 2^(x+3). 2n²–72=8n. 2n²–8n–72=0. n²–4n–36=0. Disc=16+144=160. Still not clean. Use: 2^(2x+1)–48=2^(x+4). 2n²–48=16n. 2n²–16n–48=0. n²–8n–24=0. Hmm. Try: 3^(2x+1)–81=3^(x+2). 3·(3^x)²–81=9·3^x. Let m=3^x: 3m²–9m–81=0. m²–3m–27=0. Not clean. Simplest: just use 2^(2x+1)–40=2^(x+3). n²–4n–20=0. n=(4±√96)/2=(4±4√6)/2=2±2√6. n=2+2√6≈6.899. 2^x=6.899. x=log₂(6.899)≈2.787. Not clean integer. I'll accept non-integer answer or adjust the equation to: 2^(2x+1)–24=2^(x+2). 2n²–24=4n. 2n²–4n–24=0. n²–2n–12=0. Disc=4+48=52. Still not clean. Final attempt: 2^(2x+1)–16=2^(x+3). 2n²–16=8n. n²–4n–8=0. n=2±2√3. Not integer. I'll use the straightforward version and accept x = log₂(2+2√6).

questions.text: What is the value of k needed to write 9x² – 30x + k as a perfect square?
questions.markingGuide: 9x² – 30x + k = (3x)² – 2(3x)(5) + k. Perfect square (3x–5)² needs k = 25.

questions.text: The solutions to 12/(3x – 1)² = 2 can be written in the form (1 + √a)/b and (1 – √a)/b. Find a and b.

The values of x and y satisfy:
  y – 2x = 8
  x² + 2ky = 4k
where k is a non-zero constant.

Given that only one solution exists, find k and the solution (x, y).
A quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has solutions x = 3/4 and x = –2/3. Find integer values of a, b, and c.
If p = logₐ3 and q = logₐ5, write logₐ75 in terms of p and q.

An expression for the sum of two squares is: a² + b² = (a + b)² – 2ab.

If a and b are the solutions of x² – mx + n = 0, find a² + b² in terms of m and n.
questions.markingGuide: By Vieta's: a + b = m, ab = n. a² + b² = (a+b)² – 2ab = m² – 2n.

questions.text:
A cricketer hits a ball from a crease that is 2 m above the level of the boundary rope. The ball reaches maximum height of 30 m when 80 m from the crease. A fielder standing 150 m from the crease can jump to reach 3 m high. Assume a quadratic flight path.

Will the ball clear the fielder?
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes, the ball clears the fielder. At x = 150, height ≈ 3.75 m > 3 m.
questions.markingGuide: Vertex form: y = a(x–80)² + 30. At x=0, y=2: 2 = a(6400) + 30. a = –28/6400 = –7/1600. At x=150: y = (–7/1600)(70)² + 30 = (–7)(4900)/1600 + 30 = –21.4375 + 30 = 8.5625. Since 8.56 > 3, ball clears fielder easily. Achieved = vertex form set up. Merit = finds a. Excellence = evaluates at x=150 and concludes.
